concepts.name: Classification of Nyaya and Vaisheshika within Astika Schools
key_dimensions: Distinction between Astika (orthodox) and Nastika (heterodox) schools and the criterion of Vedic acceptance
Nyaya and Vaisheshika as allied/complementary schools often studied together (Nyaya-Vaisheshika combine)
Comparison with other Astika schools: Samkhya, Yoga, Mimamsa, Vedanta — overlaps and distinctions
UPSC trap: Vaisheshika is pluralistic and realistic, NOT idealistic like Advaita Vedanta

concepts.name: Foundational Texts and Founders of Nyaya School
key_dimensions: Nyaya Sutras attributed to Gautama (also called Akshapada Gautama) — not to be confused with Gautama Buddha
Vatsyayana's Nyaya Bhashya as the primary commentary on Nyaya Sutras
Later developments: Navya-Nyaya (New Logic) school founded by Gangesa (Tattvachintamani)
UPSC trap: Gautama of Nyaya ≠ Gautama Buddha; confusion frequently tested

concepts.name: Foundational Texts and Founders of Vaisheshika School
key_dimensions: Vaisheshika Sutras attributed to Kanada (also called Uluka) — meaning and significance of the name 'Kanada' (grain-eater)
Core text: Vaisheshika Sutras (Kanada Sutras) and Prasastapada's Padarthadharmasangraha as key commentary
Relationship between Vaisheshika and atomic theory in Indian philosophy
UPSC trap: Kanada's atomic theory is philosophical/metaphysical, not empirical science — distinction critical

concepts.name: Nyaya's Theory of Pramanas (Valid Sources of Knowledge)
key_dimensions: Four Pramanas accepted by Nyaya: Pratyaksha (perception), Anumana (inference), Upamana (comparison), Shabda (testimony)
Comparison with other schools: Charvaka accepts only Pratyaksha; Samkhya accepts three; Mimamsa and Vedanta accept six
Nyaya's unique contribution of Upamana (analogy/comparison) as a distinct Pramana
UPSC trap: Nyaya accepts FOUR Pramanas — not two, not six; and Shabda here means Vedic/authoritative testimony

concepts.name: Nyaya's Theory of Anumana (Inference) and the Syllogism
key_dimensions: Five-membered syllogism (Pancavayava): Pratijna, Hetu, Udaharana, Upanaya, Nigamana — structure and purpose
Comparison with Aristotelian three-membered syllogism: similarities and key differences
Concept of Vyapti (invariable concomitance) as the logical backbone of Nyaya inference
UPSC trap: Nyaya syllogism has FIVE members, not three like Aristotle's — a frequently tested distinction

concepts.name: Vaisheshika's Seven Categories (Padarthas)
key_dimensions: Original six Padarthas by Kanada: Dravya, Guna, Karma, Samanya, Vishesha, Samavaya
Seventh category Abhava (non-existence/negation) added later by commentators
Significance of 'Vishesha' (ultimate particulars) as the category that gives the school its name
UPSC trap: Original Vaisheshika had SIX categories; Abhava as seventh was a later addition — order and names frequently tested

concepts.name: Vaisheshika's Nine Dravyas (Substances)
key_dimensions: Nine substances: Earth, Water, Fire, Air, Ether (Akasha), Time (Kala), Space (Dik), Self (Atman), Mind (Manas)
Distinction between eternal (nitya) and non-eternal (anitya) substances within the nine
Philosophical significance: Vaisheshika as a pluralistic realism — multiple ultimate substances exist
UPSC trap: Vaisheshika accepts NINE substances including Time, Space, Self, and Mind — not just five elements

concepts.name: Vaisheshika's Atomic Theory (Paramanu Vada)
key_dimensions: Atoms (Paramanu) as eternal, indivisible, and imperceptible — belonging to four elements: earth, water, fire, air
Ether, Time, Space, Self, and Mind are NOT atomic — a critical distinction
Process of atomic combination: Dyads (Dvyanuka) and Triads (Tryanuka) leading to perceptible objects
UPSC trap: Vaisheshika atomic theory is NOT the same as modern atomic theory; also Ether/Akasha is non-atomic unlike the four elements

concepts.name: Concept of Samavaya (Inseparable Relation) in Vaisheshika
key_dimensions: Samavaya as the permanent, inseparable relation between substance and quality, whole and parts, universal and particular
Distinction between Samyoga (conjunctive/separable relation) and Samavaya (inherence/inseparable relation)
Samavaya as one of the six/seven Padarthas and its ontological importance
UPSC trap: Samavaya ≠ Samyoga — Samavaya is inherence (inseparable) while Samyoga is mere contact (separable)

concepts.name: Nyaya's Concept of God (Ishvara) and Theistic Realism
key_dimensions: Nyaya provides rational/logical proofs for the existence of God (Ishvara) — unlike Samkhya which is atheistic
God as the efficient cause (Nimitta Karana) of the universe, not the material cause
Udayana's Nyayakusumanjali: systematic logical proofs for God's existence
UPSC trap: Nyaya is THEISTIC; Samkhya is ATHEISTIC/non-theistic — a classic comparison trap in UPSC

concepts.name: Nyaya's Theory of Perception (Pratyaksha) — Ordinary and Extraordinary
key_dimensions: Two types: Laukika (ordinary) — involving contact of sense organs with objects; Alaukika (extraordinary) — without normal sense contact
Three types of Alaukika perception: Samanyalakshana, Jnanalakshana, and Yogaja
Distinction between Nirvikalpa (indeterminate) and Savikalpa (determinate) perception
UPSC trap: Nyaya accepts extraordinary perception (Alaukika) unlike purely empiricist schools — this is a subtle but testable point

concepts.name: Nyaya's Theory of Liberation (Apavarga/Moksha)
key_dimensions: Moksha defined as the complete cessation of pain (Apavarga) — negative definition, not positive bliss
Path to liberation: Right knowledge (Tattvajnana) dispels false knowledge → removes attachment/aversion → stops rebirth
Comparison with Vedanta's Moksha (positive bliss of Brahman-union) vs Nyaya's Apavarga (cessation of suffering)
UPSC trap: Nyaya's Moksha is the CESSATION OF PAIN (negative concept), NOT eternal bliss — contrasts sharply with Vedanta

concepts.name: Vaisheshika's Concept of Universal (Samanya) and Particular (Vishesha)
key_dimensions: Samanya as the universal/class essence that creates similarities among individuals (e.g., 'cowness' in all cows)
Vishesha as the ultimate differentiators of eternal substances — making each atom distinct
Realist position: Universals exist independently in reality (not just in mind) — contrasts with nominalism
UPSC trap: Vaisheshika is a REALIST school regarding universals — universals have real existence, unlike Buddhist nominalism

concepts.name: Nyaya-Vaisheshika Synthesis and Their Complementary Relationship
key_dimensions: Nyaya focuses on epistemology and logic (how we know); Vaisheshika focuses on ontology/metaphysics (what exists)
Historical merger: By medieval period, the two schools were often treated as one system (Nyaya-Vaisheshika)
Shared metaphysical commitments: pluralistic realism, acceptance of external world, theism (later Vaisheshika)
UPSC trap: Nyaya = Logic/Epistemology; Vaisheshika = Metaphysics/Categories — their distinct primary contributions are testable

concepts.name: Navya-Nyaya (New Logic) School
key_dimensions: Founded by Gangesa Upadhyaya (13th century CE) with his work Tattvachintamani
Navya-Nyaya developed a precise technical language for logical analysis — influenced later Indian epistemology
Centers of Navya-Nyaya: Mithila and Nabadwip (Bengal) — geographical spread important
UPSC trap: Navya-Nyaya ≠ original Nyaya of Gautama — it is a MEDIEVAL reformation of the school with new terminology

concepts.name: Vaisheshika's Theory of Causation (Asatkaryavada)
key_dimensions: Asatkaryavada (theory of non-pre-existence of effect): the effect is NEW, not pre-existent in the cause
Contrast with Samkhya's Satkaryavada (effect pre-exists in cause) — a major philosophical debate
Implication for atomic theory: new combinations of atoms create genuinely new substances
UPSC trap: Vaisheshika = Asatkaryavada (effect is NEW); Samkhya = Satkaryavada (effect pre-exists) — a classic paired trap

concepts.name: Nyaya's Concept of Tarka (Hypothetical Reasoning) and Vitanda (Destructive Debate)
key_dimensions: Tarka as indirect reasoning/reductio ad absurdum — used to support inference but NOT an independent Pramana
Three types of debate in Nyaya: Vada (honest debate), Jalpa (disputative), Vitanda (destructive/sophistic)
Nyaya's contribution to Indian debate theory (Vadavidya) and its cultural significance
UPSC trap: Tarka is NOT a Pramana in Nyaya — it supports reasoning but is not a source of valid knowledge independently

concepts.name: Nyaya-Vaisheshika's Critique of Buddhist Philosophy
key_dimensions: Nyaya-Vaisheshika defended the reality of the external world against Buddhist idealism (Vijnanavada)
Refutation of Buddhist doctrine of momentariness (Kshanabhangavada) — Nyaya argued for enduring substances
Udayana's refutation of Buddhist atheism through logical proofs for God in Nyayakusumanjali
UPSC trap: Nyaya-Vaisheshika engaged in active philosophical polemics with Buddhism — not just parallel development

concepts.name: Concept of Atman (Self) in Nyaya-Vaisheshika
key_dimensions: Atman accepted as a distinct eternal substance (one of nine Dravyas in Vaisheshika)
Multiple individual Atmans exist — pluralistic view, contrasting with Advaita's single Brahman
Atman as the substratum of consciousness, pleasure, pain, desire, and cognition
UPSC trap: Nyaya-Vaisheshika accepts MULTIPLE individual Atmans (pluralism) ≠ Advaita (one Brahman) ≠ Buddhism (no-self/Anatman)

concepts.name: Abhava (Non-Existence) as a Category in Vaisheshika
key_dimensions: Four types of Abhava: Pragabhava (prior non-existence), Pradhvamsabhava (posterior non-existence), Anyonyabhava (mutual non-existence), Atyantabhava (absolute non-existence)
Added as the seventh Padartha to the original six by later Vaisheshika commentators
Philosophical significance: treating non-existence as a real ontological category
UPSC trap: Abhava was NOT part of Kanada's original six categories — it was a later addition; also the four subtypes are frequently tested
